display.title: Episode 27: Saved by a Miracle, Chapter 2
display.summary_short: The end of Reb Boruch's story: by following the Alter Rebbe's advice to wait a week, he escapes a deadly trap. Plus two brothers say the Shema and listeners' letters.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi opens by thanking listeners whose letters come from as far as 150 miles around New York, followed by a sponsor message and the Hakochainik march, this time with a tambourine. After a recap of Reb Boruch's story, two brothers recite the Shema in Studio 604 and tell how they bought letters in the new Sefer Torah. The story concludes: a week late, the Alter Rebbe sends Reb Boruch to the minister with a blessing. The guards rush him in, and the minister greets him with amazement. Furious about the logs, he had handed the case to the authorities, who had sent an officer to shoot Reb Boruch when he arrived that Tuesday. Because he did not come, he was saved, and in the meantime two witnesses revealed that Alex had planted the logs. Reb Boruch gets his job back with a raise, and sees how different things look through the eyes of a tzaddik. Two listeners' letters are read in the mailbox, one with coins for the pushka, and Uncle Yossi links Parshas Behaaloscha's golden menorah to the light girls bring by lighting Shabbos candles.
display.lesson: Trust the guidance of a tzaddik even when it seems strange; Hashem gives the tzaddik the power to see what we cannot.

date.note: 'Be in shul this Shabbos for Behaaloscha' (Shabbos 20 Sivan 5742); a letter dated February 19 'waited almost four months'. Matches the weekly estimate.

advisories.note: The minister reveals that an officer had been ordered to shoot Reb Boruch on sight.
A Jew falsely accused and summoned by the Russian authorities.

privacy.note: Two Shema guests and two letter writers named in full on air.
